forecast.text: World Gold Council 2025 annual central-bank survey: ~95% of respondents expect global official gold reserves to keep rising over the next 12 months and ~40% plan to add to their own reserves; drivers are de-dollarisation, geopolitical hedging and the rate environment.

cbFlow.source: IMF IRFCL official SDMX API (official reserve assets — gold holdings, FTO basis)
cbFlow.note: IMF-reporting countries only: central banks that file monthly with the IMF (non-reporters are excluded, so this runs below the WGC all-country figure). Direct from the official API; data through 2026-09 (roughly a 2-month lag).

longview.source_note: Long history: gold/silver/DXY = Yahoo Finance 20-year daily series; 10Y TIPS real yield and 10Y breakeven inflation = FRED (since 2003). Percentile = share of history at or below the current value (full history, not a rolling window).

realRate.proxyNote: Site proxy = 10Y nominal yield − CPI y/y; the gap versus the market rate (TIPS) is a mix of inflation expectations and liquidity premium

drivers.name: Treasury yield trend
drivers.reason: 10Y yield -39bp over 20d (flat) to 4.87%; real rate (10Y−CPI) ≈1.17%: yields fell — lower real rates and more room to cut, bullish gold | level damping 52-week percentile 54% (elevated) ×0.94; quasi-real rate +1.17% (real opportunity cost of holding gold) ×0.75 → combined ×0.70

drivers.name: Cross-asset capital flows
drivers.reason: Equities (S&P -5.6%) and gold (-3.1%) fell while long Treasuries (TLT +5.0%) rose — capital is rotating out of stocks and gold INTO bonds: at high yields, bonds offer certain income while gold is sold first as a non-yielding asset

drivers.name: Policy pricing
drivers.reason: Polymarket hike odds 77.0%: hawkish pricing is bearish

drivers.name: Oil→CPI transmission
drivers.reason: Brent -5.8% over 30d (-2.9% over 90d) to $98.32: the 30d direction dominates — oil→CPI→rates pressure

drivers.name: Risk sentiment (VIX)
drivers.reason: VIX +73.0% over 20d to 25.6: risk-off rising — flows seek safe havens such as gold (bullish) | Note: gold fell alongside risk assets, so a higher VIX does NOT mean haven money is buying gold; the real signal sits in Cross-asset capital flows, so this factor is heavily damped

drivers.name: Inflation direction
drivers.reason: CPI YoY +0.3pp over 2m to 3.7%: rising = tightening pressure (bearish) (direction-only, capped ±60); the level is still above the 2% target (see the 'Inflation constraint' row)

drivers.name: Central-bank gold buying
drivers.reason: IMF-reporting central banks net-bought +305 t over the last 12 months (2025-10–2026-09) and the WGC survey has 95% expecting more buying: structurally bullish (non-reporting banks excluded)

drivers.name: US debt burden
drivers.reason: Federal debt at 121.2% of GDP (2026-Q2, +3.0pp y/y), net interest outlays $1329B annualised (2026-Q3): high debt and interest costs squeeze policy room — fiscal-dominance and debasement concerns are structurally bullish for gold

drivers.name: US Dollar Index (DXY)
drivers.reason: DXY -0.29% over 20d to 102.286: weaker dollar supports gold

events.title: October CPI release
reasons: CPI momentum +0.15pp/m over 2m (3.4→3.4→3.7): disinflation continues but decelerates (decay 0.6)
Core PCE 3.12% still above 2%: rent/services stickiness supports the core
ADP just +86k and U-Mich confidence 51.0: weak demand caps services inflation

events.title: 2026-Q3 GDP final · October PCE
reasons: Weak real-activity signals vs initial print (U-Mich 51.0, soft ADP) tilt slightly downward
If core PCE keeps rising (3.12%→?), it decides the December meeting

events.title: November payrolls release
reasons: Revision tracker: October initial +165k → now +165k (noisy initial prints; range widened to ±50k)

events.title: Year-end FOMC decision
events.est: The last action window of the year
reasons: Depends on the core PCE path from here: falling keeps cuts on the table; rising extends tightening

events.title: FOMC rate decision
events.prob: hike 77.0% · hold 21.5% · cut 1.5% (Polymarket market pricing · 2026-12-10 meeting)
reasons: Polymarket market pricing · 2026-12-10 meeting: hike 77.0% / hold 21.5% / cut 1.5%
Core PCE up +0.08pp over 3m to 3.12%: inflation constraint favors tightening
Jobs still resilient (October +165k; October initial +165k); with 2026-Q3 GDP at 3.4% the cost of tightening is manageable
Election politics raise the political cost of tightening → AI leans hold vs the market

events.title: Midterm election day
reasons: Incumbent needs a good economy and rising stocks; fiscal/regulatory tilt eases pre-election

meta.source_policy: Every field carries its own source and asOf/date; when an upstream source fails, the last successful value is kept and flagged stale=true.
meta.disclaimer: Same figures and definitions as the site, from the same snapshot and the same code path, checked programmatically; not investment advice.
meta.attribution: Please credit xaudaily.com as the source.
meta.citation_en: Source: Gold Data Reading, xaudaily.com — https://xaudaily.com/
meta.channel_param: You may append ?src=<your-app-name>: such requests bypass the CDN cache (no-store) and let us count usage per channel — recommended.
meta.update_schedule: Full refresh at 06:30 / 22:40 JST; gold and Shanghai gold tick roughly every 30 minutes.
meta.stability: Within v1, fields are only ever added — never renamed or removed; a breaking change would bump the schema version.

translation.note: This payload is the Chinese payload with string values rendered in English; all numbers come from the same snapshot. Dynamic prose (driver reasons, event estimates) reuses the bilingual fields authored alongside the Chinese text.
